s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath with evidence of cardiac and respiratory compromise
salient_findings: Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function
Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli
Elevated troponin and N-terminal pro brain-type natriuretic peptide levels
key_facts: 82-year-old man
History of coronary artery disease with stent placement 10 years ago
History of surgically treated colon cancer
Episodes of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath began one day before admission
Heart rate: 114 beats/min
Blood pressure: 94/62 mm Hg
Oxygen saturation: 91% on 4 L/min of supplemental oxygen
Respiratory rate: 28 breaths per minute
Troponin I level: 0.135 µg/L (peaked at 0.499 µg/L)
D-dimer level: >109.52 nmol/L
N-terminal pro brain-type natriuretic peptide level: 562.21 pmol/L
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function
CT Angiogram showed acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Embolism
shortlist.why_kept: CT Angiogram showed acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli

shortlist.label: Acute Cor Pulmonale
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function and pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Crisis
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction

shortlist.label: Cardiogenic Shock
shortlist.why_kept: Hypotension and evidence of cardiac compromise

shortlist.label: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hypoxemia and bilateral infiltrates on imaging

raw.rationale: The CT Angiogram showed acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli, which directly supports the diagnosis of Pulmonary Embolism. The patient's symptoms of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath, along with the elevated D-dimer level and troponin I level, are also consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Cor Pulmonale
rejected.why: While the patient has a dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function, which could suggest Acute Cor Pulmonale, the primary issue is the pulmonary embolism causing the right ventricular strain, not the other way around.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Crisis
rejected.why: Pulmonary hypertension is present, but it is secondary to the acute pulmonary embolism, not the primary cause of the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic Shock
rejected.why: The patient's low blood pressure and elevated heart rate could suggest cardiogenic shock, but the primary cause of these symptoms appears to be the pulmonary embolism, not a primary cardiac issue.

rejected.label: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
rejected.why: The follow-up CT shows an alveolar filling process, but this appears to be a secondary complication rather than the primary diagnosis, which is pulmonary embolism.
